# The archsimd feature check must dominate the vector block through
# a conditional branch: the AVX2 call, the test of its result, and
# the jump to the scalar block appear in that order, the instruction
# after the jump is the vector prologue (so the jump targets the
# scalar loop), and the masked tail load of the vector block follows.
# Sums stay correct with the check forced false (scalar path) and at
# v3 (check omitted).
[!GOARCH:amd64] skip 'gate branch objdump needs amd64'

env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local
env GOEXPERIMENT=simd
env GOAMD64=v1
cd m

logos build -o $WORK/exe .
go tool objdump -s '^main\.sumI32$' $WORK/exe
stdout '(?s)CALL simd/archsimd\.X86Features\.AVX2\(SB\).*TESTL AL, AL.*JE'
# The instruction after the feature-false jump is the vector prologue:
# the jump targets the scalar loop. Swapped targets keep JE and
# VPMASKMOVD but put scalar code here.
stdout '(?s)CALL simd/archsimd\.X86Features\.AVX2\(SB\)[^\n]*\n[^\n]*TESTL AL, AL[ \t]*\n[^\n]*JE 0x[0-9a-f]+[ \t]*\n[^\n]*VPXOR'
stdout 'VPMASKMOVD'

env GODEBUG=cpu.avx2=off
logos run .
# The program observes the check itself: false here proves the sums
# below ran through the scalar loop the jump above targets.
stdout '^avx2 false$'
stdout '^sums ok$'

env GODEBUG=
env GOAMD64=v3
logos run .
stdout '^sums ok$'

-- m/go.mod --
module example.com/gatebranch

go 1.27

-- m/main.lgo --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"simd/archsimd"
)

//go:noinline
func sumI32(xs []int32) int32 { return xs.sum() }

func oracleI32(xs []int32) int32 {
	t := int32(0)
	for _, v := range xs {
		t += v
	}
	return t
}

func main() {
	fmt.Println("avx2", archsimd.X86.AVX2())
	xs := make([]int32, 70)
	for i := range xs {
		xs[i] = int32(i*7 - 100)
	}
	if sumI32(xs) != oracleI32(xs) {
		panic("int32 sum mismatch")
	}
	fmt.Println("sums ok")
}
